posts.text: If your wallet is small and it’s still not growing, read this. You don’t need bigger trades. You need better risk management. Let’s say you have a $200 wallet. Before entering any trade, decide one thing first: “How much am I okay losing if this trade is wrong?” For example, fix your maximum risk at $5 per trade. Now don’t randomly put $5 as margin and choose 20x leverage. That’s not how it works. First find your entry, then find the technical stop-loss the level where your trade idea becomes invalid. Suppose your SL is 5% away. Maximum risk = $5 SL distance = 5% Position size = $5 ÷ 5% = $100 Only after this calculate the leverage according to the margin you want to use. If you use $10 margin: $100 ÷ $10 = 10x leverage So if the 5% SL gets hit, your planned loss is around $5, not your whole account. posts.text: Things get really clear when the market breaks a major zone. How? You basically have two options. Either you wait for price to come down to a very important zone and give you a deeper discount before buying, or you wait for the market to reclaim the levels it broke with strong volume. So you get two simple plans: Plan 1: The market shows strength, picks up volume, and reclaims the levels it has broken. Plan 2: You get a deeper pullback. Altcoins drop another 10–15–20%, BTC goes through another capitulation, and then you look for buying opportunities. That's it. Two plans. Either the market shows strength, or you get a deeper discount. Nothing in between. Just relax, sit on the sidelines, and watch the market. Whichever setup plays out first, we'll react accordingly. Until then, just watch the market and let it do its thing.
